sources.quote: The canonical VNP-complete problems are the permanent and the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial
sources.rationale: The objects under study. They are fixed by the problem and not chosen by the authors.

sources.quote: Which of the two hypotheses holds may depend on the field.
sources.rationale: The field is given. Its characteristic and which of the two hypotheses holds over it are facts about it, not choices of the authors.

sources.quote: An arithmetic circuit over a commutative ring 𝑅 is a finite list of polynomials over 𝑅, each of which is a variable, a constant from 𝑅, or the sum or the product of two earlier entries of the list
sources.rationale: Definitions and the size convention are fixed by the authors.

sources.quote: The proof consists of two cases, the contracting case and the flat case, according to which of two technical hypotheses (described next) holds.
sources.rationale: The split into a flat and a contracting case is a construction of the authors.

sources.quote: both times through an explicit form of Valiant’s completeness theorem [Val79]
sources.rationale: Published results that the authors import. Treated like an external pretrained component.

sources.quote: The proofs in this paper were found and written by AI.
sources.rationale: The system that produced the proofs, chosen by whoever ran the study. The attribution is taken from the paper; the paper does not describe how the model was run.

sources.quote: The Lean proof assumes nothing beyond Mathlib.
sources.rationale: Proof assistant version, library commit and standard axioms chosen and imported by the authors.

sources.quote: Comparator accepted them against Challenge.lean, rechecking the proofs with Lean’s kernel and with the independently written checker nanoda.
sources.rationale: Outputs of proof checkers as the paper reports them. They are read off, not chosen. The auditor did not see or rerun them.

sources.quote: Whether the statements say what is meant was judged only by AI readers.
sources.rationale: The only reported check that the Lean statements mean what the paper says.

ops.name: prove_one_case_holds
ops.quote: We assume that the contracting hypothesis fails and derive the flat one.
ops.rationale: Theorem 2.2 (D.2). The model is an input because it wrote the printed proof.

ops.name: reduce_to_clause_sums
ops.quote: a circuit for the permanent gives, by substitution, circuits of about the same size for them.
ops.rationale: The only place where the permanent, or the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, enters. For the permanent it needs 2 to be invertible.

ops.name: flat_case_bound
ops.quote: this gives the bound of Theorem 1.1 in the flat case

ops.name: state_main_results_in_lean
ops.quote: We now print the file Statement.lean of the Lean development, which imports Mathlib and nothing else and states the main results so that a reader can check that it correctly formalizes the statements in this paper.

ops.name: recheck_with_kernel
ops.quote: The theorems of Solution depend on no axioms other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, as scripts/PrintAxioms.lean prints.

ops.name: match_lean_statements_to_paper
ops.quote: In the namespace Solution the theorems mainTheorem, mainTheoremApprox, separation and separationClosure have exactly the types MainTheorem, MainTheoremApprox, Separation and SeparationClosure
ops.rationale: The checked Lean theorems count as the paper's results only if the Lean statements mean what the paper says.

ops.name: contracting_case_bound
ops.quote: The proofs of Proposition I.1, Theorem H.2(d), (e), Theorem J.3 and Proposition N.4 describe machines and programs and account for their sizes and running times.
ops.rationale: The Lean development is an input because the printed proofs of these statements only describe the machines and programs.

ops.name: combine_two_cases
ops.quote: Hence the smaller of 𝑐′ and 𝑐′′ serves as the constant 𝑐 of the theorem.
ops.rationale: The bound as worded is derived under each of the two hypotheses, and Theorem D.2 says that one of them holds, so the conclusion does not change with the case. The derivation in the contracting case is complete only in Lean.

ops.name: extend_to_all_fields
ops.quote: This appendix proves the lower bound of Theorem L.1 over every field, with a constant that does not depend on the field (Theorem M.3)

ops.name: separate_classes
ops.quote: By Theorem M.3 it is not in VP.

claims.statement: Every arithmetic circuit for the m x m permanent over the reals, and over every field of characteristic other than two, has more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates for all sufficiently large m; the same holds for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial over every field; hence VP is not equal to VNP over every field.
claims.quote: We prove that every arithmetic circuit that computes the permanent of an 1/3 𝑚 × 𝑚 matrix over the reals has more than 𝑚𝑐(log 𝑚) gates, for some constant 𝑐 > 0 and all sufficiently large 𝑚. The same bound holds over every field of characteristic other than two and, for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial in place of the permanent, the same bound holds over every field. Hence VP ̸= VNP over every field.

hypotheses.quote: Of the field we use only that 2 ̸= 0, for the matrix entries
hypotheses.rationale: The claim limits the bound for the permanent to the reals and to fields of characteristic other than two. For every field it uses the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, whose reduction needs no division.

hypotheses.quote: The constant 𝑚0 in our theorems is not effective
hypotheses.rationale: The theorem holds for m at least m0. The claim is worded for all sufficiently large m and gives no value for the threshold, so the condition holds for the target as worded. The threshold is not effective and depends on the characteristic.

hypotheses.quote: Over every field k at least one of the two hypotheses of Definition 2.1 holds, that is, one of the two cases occurs.
hypotheses.rationale: Theorem 2.2 (D.2). Its printed proof is in Appendix D, which the paper lists among the proofs meant to be complete, and it has the Lean theorem thm_alt. The claim needs only that one case holds; the paper says it does not know which.

hypotheses.quote: That these do exactly what is claimed can be verified only in the Lean development, and each of these four statements is followed by a formalization note that says so.
hypotheses.rationale: Not shown by the printed proofs. The paper reports that these steps are proved in the Lean development and that the proofs were rechecked by Lean's kernel and by a second checker. Discharged on that report only; the auditor did not see the development.

hypotheses.quote: The family (HC𝑚 ) is in VNP [Val79], as one sees by summing over one-hot codes of the places that the vertices take on the cycle
hypotheses.rationale: Needed for the last sentence of the claim. Given by a citation with a one-line argument, and by the Lean theorem cor_allclasses.

hypotheses.quote: Whether the statements say what is meant was judged only by AI readers. No human mathematician has checked the development, the statement file or the proofs.
hypotheses.rationale: The paper says that every main result rests on Lean, so the Lean statements must mean what the claim says. The paper reports only a judgement by AI readers and says that no human mathematician has checked the statement file. It says so openly, so this is a declared bet. The statement file for the main results is printed in Section 3.

claims.notes: The target is the last node of the derivation, so the hypotheses cover all three sentences of the claim. Which of the two cases holds is unknown and is not a hypothesis, because the claim needs only that one of them holds.

claims.statement: The main results of the paper have been stated and proved in Lean. The paper attributes their discovery to an internal research Claude model.
claims.quote: The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model and has been formalized in Lean.

hypotheses.quote: it states four propositions: MainTheorem is Theorem M.3, MainTheoremApprox is the first assertion of Theorem N.5, Separation is Corollary M.4, and SeparationClosure is the second assertion of Theorem N.5.
hypotheses.rationale: The statement file printed in Section 3 states the results that the abstract calls the result. Remark N.6, the one numbered statement that is not formalized, is not among them.

hypotheses.quote: Comparator accepted them against Challenge.lean, rechecking the proofs with Lean’s kernel and with the independently written checker nanoda.
hypotheses.rationale: A check that the paper reports, with the tools named. The auditor did not rerun it.

hypotheses.rationale: Reported in Section 3 and in Appendix Q.1. The auditor did not rerun it.

hypotheses.rationale: The paper reports only a judgement by AI readers and says that no human mathematician has checked the statement file. It says so openly, so this is a declared bet. The statement file for the main results is printed in Section 3.

The paper gives no account of how the model was run or of any human part in the discovery. It is recorded as the source node claudeModel and is neither supported nor contradicted by this record.

claims.statement: Every main result depends on the Lean development, because the printed proofs of four statements of the contracting case only describe machines and programs.
claims.quote: Consequently the contracting case, and with it every main result, rests on Lean at these points.
claims.notes: Added so that the record checks whether everything the main result is obtained through is stated in the paper. Every source upstream of the main result is stated somewhere in the paper, so all are listed as declared.
